7 23-03-2023 The applicant/appellant, vide this interim application has renewed his prayer for grant of bail.
He is convicted of the offence punishable under Section 376 (2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code as well as under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
He is also convicted of the offence under Section 10 of the POCSO Act.

The applicant/appellant is sentenced to suffer a rigorous imprisonment for 12 years apart from the imposition of fine for the offence punishable under section 376 (2)(i) of the I.P.C. No Patna High Court CR. APP (DB) No.1474 of 2018(7) dt.23-03-2023
separate sentence was awarded for the offence under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
He is sentenced to suffer a rigorous imprisonment for five years for the offence punishable under Section 10 of the POCSO Act.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the appellant;
He argued that substantive sentences are directed to run concurrently and as such the appellant/applicant has virtually undergone for half of the sentence imposed on him.
It is further argued that evidence adduced by the prosecution is not trustworthy.
Medical evidence is not supporting the case of prosecution.

The victim of the crime in question in cross-examination has accepted the fact that in a happy mood she returned from work place where according to the prosecution case, penetrative sexual assault was committed on her.
We are also heard, the learned APP opposed the prayer for grant of bail.
We have considered the submissions so advanced and we have also perused the material placed on record including deposition of prosecution witnesses.
We are alive to the fact that for making out the offence of penetrative sexual assault, it is not at all necessary that medical evidence must support the Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1474 of 2018(7) dt.23-03-2023 prosecution case.

However,
in the case in hand, victim of the crime in question who is stated to be 13-14 years old has categorically stated that the appellant/applicant had penetrated her and had also discharged semen.
So for as medical evidence is concerned, the attending medical officer has stated upon medical examination of the victim female child that he had not noticed swelling, bleeding and tenderness.
There was no tear at the private parts of the victim and her hymen was also intact.
Cross-examination of the victim female child is suggestive of the fact that she is tutored witness as she has accepted that she has deposed whatever was told to her by the prosecutor.
She further admitted in her cross examination that she had gone for attending the work in a happy mood and had also returned from there in a happy mood.
It is the case of the prosecution that the victim female child had gone for domestic work at the house of one Shekhar Singh, where appellant/applicant had committed penetrative sexual assault on her.
We are also noted that the incident in question alleged took place on 18.06.2017.
The FIR in respect of the same was lodged on 20.06.2017.
First informant who happens to be father of victim female child is not examined by the prosecution.
Moreover, the appellant/applicant has already undergone half of Patna High Court CR.
APP (DB) No.1474 of 2018(7) dt.23-03-2023 the sentence imposed on him.
There is no likelihood of the appeal being heard.

In this view of the matter, we see no reason to refuse bail to the applicant and as such the orders:
Therefore the order:-
I. The application is allowed.
II. The substantive sentence of imprisonment imposed on the appellant till the disposal of the instant appeals is suspended and he is directed to be released on bail on executing P.R. bond of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) and on furnishing two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned 1st Additional District & Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge POCSO, Muzaffarpur/concerned Court Kali Singh @ Kalicharan Singh @ Sudhakar ... vs The State Of Bihar on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70125194/
2 in connection with Sadar P.S. Case No. 312 of 2017.
